title: Senior Software Engineer, Agent Policy Fabric
description: The Agentic Safety Engineering team is building Agent Policy Fabric (APF), an enterprise governance layer for AI agents. APF combines signed policy, runtime verification, policy projection, credential mediation, and audit records to help govern the actions agents take across enterprise systems. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help turn the APF proof of concept into diligent production software. You will build, implement, test, and operate features in policy verification, runtime integration, or conformance testing. Working with experienced platform and security engineers, you will own a defined feature or subsystem and help ensure that policy decisions are accurate, integrations are reliable, and failures are handled safely! Join us! What You'll Be Doing: Build policy-verification features: Implement components of the Runtime Policy Verifier and authorization APIs, including signed policy validation, freshness and revocation checks, rollback protection, and binding decisions to the correct subject and runtime context, following reviewed security contracts. Implement policy projection: Translate canonical APF policy into runtime-specific rules and adapter constraints. Handle unsupported policies and partial updates safely so runtimes admit work only when the required policy has been accepted. Develop runtime integrations: Work with OpenShell and other runtime engineers to implement and test agreed interfaces for policy consumption, runtime context, admission decisions, and audit events. Document interface behavior and raise gaps or conflicting assumptions for resolution. Strengthen correctness and conformance: Build fixtures, compatibility tests, negative tests, and property or fuzz tests that exercise policy behavior, integration boundaries, and failure paths. Investigate defects and turn findings into regression coverage. Deliver production-ready components: Add observability, measure performance, debug reliability issues, and contribute to rollout plans and operational documentation for the components you own. Contribute technical judgment: Write focused design documents, explain implementation tradeoffs, participate in code and security reviews, and work with platform, Identity, and Product Security partners to resolve issues within your scope. Help the team deliver: Break work into achievable turning points, communicate dependencies and risks, review code, and share knowledge with other engineers. What We Need To See: Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience, with 5+ years of relevant industry experience in systems software, backend services, distributed systems, security engineering, or policy infrastructure. Strong programming skills in at least one of Rust, Go, C++, or Python, with experience delivering maintainable, tested production code. Experience building and delivering services or systems components, including API design, integration, debugging, and error handling. Practical experience implementing security control

Two kinds of people fit this role. The full-stack designer who's dreamed something up, designed it, built it, and launched it end to end. Or the strong front-end engineer with real design taste, someone who codes for a living but has defensible opinions about type, layout, motion, and information density. We care about the combination, not which side you started on. Turn design mocks (yours or others’) into pixel-perfect, production-ready frontends using modern web tech. title: Head of People & Organizational Development
description: Location: Remote, within 6 hours of US Eastern Time About SPUN SPUN (Society for the Protection of Underground Networks) is a startup NGO with a mission to map and protect the mycorrhizal fungal networks that regulate Earth’s climate and ecosystems. These fungi draw down approximately 13 billion tons of CO2 each year, yet they have been largely overlooked by science, policy, and practice. Since our founding in 2021, we’ve built a global data platform to make these invisible networks measurable. Through our Underground Explorers program and network of over 700 Science Associates across more than 80 countries, with the majority in the Global South, we generate high-resolution biodiversity maps and ML-powered tools that integrate mycorrhizal data into climate, conservation, restoration, and land management decisions. Our work spans laboratory research, data science, and robotics through to locally led field applications, and we’ve begun working with policymakers and restoration practitioners to apply our findings on the ground. With strong backing from leading foundations and growing momentum in international policy circles, we’re now at an inflection point: scaling these efforts across more landscapes, institutions, and countries over the long term. That next phase calls for new capabilities. We’re strengthening our data science and impact strategy capabilities alongside our research, and have recently brought in leaders in global policy and impact, partnerships and adoption, and restoration science. Over the next two to three years, we expect to add people at every level, from directors to managers and coordinators. Doing this efficiently, across new disciplines and with a team spread across many countries, is a real organizational challenge. The Opportunity We’re looking for a Head of People & Organizational Development to shape how SPUN works as it grows. This is not a traditional HR role. Day-to-day HR administration will sit with a dedicated Operations Manager. Your focus is the organization itself: how our people collaborate, make decisions, develop, and use the tools available to them to do their best work. You will work closely with senior leadership across three connected areas: Ways of working. Design the structures, rhythms, and practices that keep a distributed, multidisciplinary team aligned and moving quickly. That covers how decisions get made and how knowledge gets shared. It also covers how scientists, data scientists, policy specialists, and partnership leads work together toward shared goals. Tools and technology. Shape the tools we rely on so they actually serve the work. This includes AI, which we believe can help expand what a small, distributed organization can accomplish in research, operations, and partnerships, but caution is also needed. The goal is not simply rolling out new tools—it is building the skills, judgment, and confidence to use them well without compromising scientific integrity. Culture and leadership. Help o

In this role, you will help power a deeply coordinated care team, partnering with registered dietitians (RDs), nurse practitioners (NPs), physicians, and care operations, to deliver comprehensive, longitudinal support to patients. You'll provide therapy to patients navigating chronic disease and behavior change; support emotional, behavioral, and mental health needs that affect metabolic outcomes; and help ensure patients receive the right intervention at the right time. We handle all administrative, insurance, billing, patient acquisition, and scheduling so you can focus entirely on high-quality, thoughtful therapy and supporting meaningful lifestyle and behavior change. About Us Nourish was founded to address a fundamental failure in the U.S. healthcare system: the rapid rise of chronic disease, which affects hundreds of millions of Americans and drives the majority of healthcare spending. Nourish has built the largest insurance-covered nutrition therapy platform in the country, connecting 10,000+ registered dietitians with patients nationwide through a seamless AI-native experience. We are now building the next chapter of Nourish : an integrated metabolic care model that brings together nutrition, lifestyle, behavioral interventions, and physician-led medical management into a single coordinated patient experience. If you're passionate about integrated care and excited to transform the healthcare system, we'd love to work with you. Our Clinical Philosophy Our approach to care is grounded in meeting patients where they are and using evidence-based practices to drive long-term lifestyle, behavioral, and metabolic change. Our interdisciplinary care team provides personalized, in-depth, expert-level care to patients from any and all backgrounds. We measure quality of outcomes against each patient's individual goals, coordinate seamlessly across care teams (RDs, NPs, physicians, behavioral health providers, outside providers), and continuously refine our approach through data, feedback, and innovation. Why Join Nourish Help solve a massive problem - hundreds of millions of Americans have metabolic conditions (diabetes, obesity, fatty liver, heart disease risk), yet most do not receive comprehensive, coordinated care Flexible schedule - you set your own hours around your weekly availability commitment (25+ hours full-time, 5+ hours part-time) and practice fully remotely W2 employment with benefits - 401(k), paid time off, and an education stipend. Full-time therapists also receive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Start seeing patients fast - on average, therapists joining Nourish start seeing patients in just one week, and our dedicated onboarding and credentialing teams will be with you every step of the way. Focus on patients

title: Applied Research Scientist, World Model
description: About the team Zillow has the richest housing market data in the industry. You help us build out a foundational model that leverages a representation of who is in the market, what they’ll pay, and how that demand clears against supply. The Agentic Foundations team is a focused group of 15–20 applied scientists within Zillow’s broader Agentic AI organization, building the foundational AI technologies that power the next generation of home shopping experiences. This Principal Applied Scientist will help build the Zillow World Model: a single, uncertainty-aware model of the housing market that ties together supply, demand and macro conditions such as mortgage rates and policy. Today, bespoke models like Zestimate, Time-to-Pending and Listing Soon each answer one question well. The foundational “World” Model aims to answer the multi-step “what if” questions consumers actually ask, such as “If I list at $500K, when will it sell?” or “I want at least $800K; what should I list at?”, as consistent projections of one market state, and to serve those answers to Voyager, Zillow’s AI Mode, as a tool. This is a very new field and an open-ended research effort. You will partner with the World Model working group (listing-state modeling, market simulation and evaluation) and with product, engineering, platform and data teams. Zillow observes both sides of the housing market at a depth no one else can, so this work can directly help guide users toward their goals. About the role Build the demand layer of the World Model: turn large-scale shopper behavior (search, engagement, session trajectories) into structured demand representations, including explicit attention-to-demand conversion. Design and train latent state-space, multi-tower and/or sequential dynamics models with calibrated uncertainty that support multi-step rollouts, forward planning (“if I do X, what happens?”) and backward planning (“I want X; what should I do?”). Estimate willingness-to-pay, per-home demand curves and market clearing dynamics, connecting learned representations to economic quantities. Apply causal identification in observational data and define where the model must abstain because a correlation does not support a “what-if” claim. Contribute to the World Model evaluation battery: state probes, calibrated multi-target forecasts, rollout drift, causal checks and out-of-regime replays. Independently drive ambiguous research end-to-end, and provide technical leadership and mentorship in translating state-of-the-art research into production impact. This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. title: Consultant: Tax and Non-Tax Incentives for Mining Downstream Viability Projects:
description: The International Institute for Sustainable Development is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world. IISD hosts the Secretariat of the Intergovernmental Forum on Mining, Minerals, Metals and Sustainable Development (IGF). The IGF's Global Mining Tax Initiative (GMTI) helps countries to increase mining revenues for sustainable development. Drawing on broad experience working with IGF member governments, the Secretariat offers this specialized and comprehensive program covering fiscal policy for the entire mining value chain, from exploration and development to mining, processing, mineral sales, and mine closure. The GMTI focuses on all aspects of fiscal policy, including taxes, royalties, and financial modelling, and has developed particular expertise on the fiscal treatment of mineral beneficiation and downstream processing. The Challenge As demand for critical minerals accelerates with the energy transition, a growing number of resource-rich countries are moving to capture more of the value chain domestically and attract investment. Whilst a variety of fiscal and non-fiscal tools are available, many resource-rich countries offer tax and non-tax incentives to attract investment into downstream mineral processing, from smelting and refining to further stages of value addition. These incentives can include corporate income tax holidays, accelerated depreciation, royalty relief, value-added tax and import duty exemptions, energy subsidies, infrastructure provision, export restrictions or differentiated export taxes on unprocessed ore, and guaranteed offtake arrangements. Governments introduce these measures with the aim of capturing more value domestically, creating jobs, and building industrial capacity. However, the fiscal and non-fiscal cost of these incentives is rarely tracked systematically, and there is limited evidence on whether they actually influence investment decisions or simply reward projects that would have gone ahead regardless. Downstream processing economics are also heavily shaped by global market conditions, such as smelting overcapacity and depressed treatment and refining charges, that incentives alone cannot offset. Governments are often left weighing significant revenue foregone against uncertain and long-dated returns in jobs, value addition, and industrial development. Our Response To help governments make better-informed decisions on this trade-off, the IGF is developing a practice note assessing the short-, medium-, and long-term impact of tax incentives for mining downstream viability projects. Our solutions enable customers across utilities, telecommunications, government, infrastructure and commercial sectors to manage assets, optimise workflows and make smarter, data-driven decisions. We combine industry expertise with powerful geospatial technologies to deliver real-world outcomes for our customers. As we continue to grow, we are looking for a Senior Geospatial Consultant to join our Professional Services team. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced consultant who enjoys solving complex data challenges, working closely with customers, and delivering high-quality geospatial solutions. We welcome applications from candidates based in both the United Kingdom and Ireland with the opportunity to be based remotely or hybrid working from our Cambridge head office. You will play a key role in project delivery, leading technical workstreams, engaging directly with customers, and supporting the development of less experienced team members. You will help organisations improve the quality, accessibility and value of their spatial data while contributing to the successful delivery of strategic programmes. We use the SFIA framework to assess competencies and expect to appoint this role at Level 3-4, depending on experience, with opportunities for progression as your responsibilities and expertise grow. The successful candidate will work across a range of technologies, with a particular focus on FME as a core platform for data integration, transformation and automation. Experience with enterprise GIS platforms and spatial databases will also be valuable. Further training in our own complementary data and application products will be provided. Travel to customer locations may occasionally be required. Due to the nature of our work it is essential that candidates are able and willing to obtain and maintain UK Security Check (SC) Clearance. Key Responsibilities L ead the delivery of geospatial consultancy projects from discovery through to implementation. Design and implement data transformation, migration and integration workflows. AI is a core part of how we work . AI can already produce content quickly and efficiently. What we need is someone with the experience, strong editorial judgment, and intuition to turn AI-generated content into high-quality, valuable content that resonates with our readers and delivers real business results. We’re looking for someone who has experience working with a small team of skilled writers, setting high editorial standards, and making content successful. You should know what good writing looks like, understand why certain content works, and be able to improve it. What You’ll Work On Content strategy and editorial direction – identify what content we should create, for whom, and why. Content quality and editing – review, improve, and refine content to make it clear, engaging, accurate, and valuable. AI-assisted content creation – use AI tools and workflows to produce high-quality content efficiently while maintaining strong editorial standards. Content performance – track results, understand what makes content successful, and use data to improve it. Content experiments – test new ideas, formats, and approaches, learn from failures, and build on what works. Collaboration with marketing and product teams – understand our products, customers, and business goals to make sure our content supports them. What We’re Looking For You’ve managed small teams of skilled writers and know how to improve and maintain high content quality. You have excellent editing and copywriting skills. You can easily spot what works in content and what needs improvement. You know how to use AI effectively to create and edit content. You’re comfortable working with metrics and taking responsibility for content performance. You use data to understand what works and what doesn't. You have strong editorial intuition built through years of experience. You’re comfortable trying new ideas, making decisions, and checking the results. You’re curious and want to understand our products, customers, and business. You’re hands-on and independent. You can take ownership of your work without detailed instructions. You have experience with technology, software, SaaS, or technical content. We are especially interested in people who have spent years working in high-quality editorial environments, where great writing, strong editorial judgment, and measurable results are essential. We’re not looking for someone whose main experience is managing large volumes of low-quality content. We want someone who knows how to make good content exceptional.
